ModuleName: 8 - Introduction to JSON and Using It in the Browser

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Outlines the module's core topics—including JSON definitions, syntax, data types, parsing with JSON.parse(), stringifying with JSON.stringify(), and fetching JSON in the browser—serving as a navigational overview for learners and instructors to see what the module covers and in what order.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: An overview page listing all topics covered in the module — JSON definition, syntax, parsing, stringifying, fetching with Fetch API and XMLHttpRequest, and displaying data — giving learners and instructors a navigational outline of what the module addresses.

Artifacts.Name: What is JSON?
Artifacts.Description: A reading that defines JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) as a lightweight, plain-text format for representing structured data, explaining its origins, its role in web data interchange, and why it is widely adopted, giving learners a conceptual foundation before working with JSON in code.

Artifacts.Name: JSON Syntax and Structure
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains JSON's syntax rules and structural elements — objects, arrays, key-value pairs, and supported data types — so learners understand how well-formed JSON is written and can read or author valid JSON documents.

Artifacts.Name: Parsing JSON in JavaScript
Artifacts.Description: A reading that covers how to use JSON.parse() to convert a JSON string received from a server or API into a usable JavaScript object, including common pitfalls and error handling, so learners can work with incoming JSON data in their applications.

Artifacts.Name: Stringifying JavaScript Objects to JSON
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains how to use JSON.stringify() to convert in-memory JavaScript objects into JSON-formatted strings for sending over a network, saving to storage, or sharing with external systems, including options for formatting output.

Artifacts.Name: Fetching JSON Data with the Fetch API
Artifacts.Description: A reading that teaches learners how to use the browser's Fetch API to make HTTP requests and retrieve JSON data from servers or public APIs, covering the promise-based workflow, response parsing, and error handling in a modern JavaScript context.

Artifacts.Name: Fetching JSON Data with XMLHttpRequest
Artifacts.Description: A reading that introduces XMLHttpRequest (XHR) as the legacy browser mechanism for making asynchronous HTTP requests to fetch JSON data, explaining its event-driven workflow so learners understand how older codebases and pre-Fetch environments handle JSON retrieval.

Artifacts.Name: Displaying JSON Data in a Web Page
Artifacts.Description: A reading that walks learners through the process of taking parsed JSON data and dynamically rendering it into a web page using DOM manipulation techniques, bridging the gap between raw data and a visible, user-facing interface.
